details: Imagine guiding a billion-dollar spacecraft toward the rim of Shackleton Crater at the Lunar South Pole. Your solar arrays are bathed in near-continuous golden sunlight, guaranteeing vital electrical power—yet the moment your landing legs touch the regolith, mission control goes silent. A jagged mountain ridge stands directly between your antenna and Earth. You have full electricity, and zero communication. At the Lunar South Pole—the primary destination for NASA’s Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) and Artemis programs—this is not a hypothetical edge case; it is an unforgiving orbital reality. Because the Moon’s axial tilt is just , sunlight grazes polar peaks at razor-thin elevation angles , casting kilometer-long shadows across craters while Earth oscillates low along the horizon due to lunar libration. Legacy mission-planning suites like NASA Quickmap and JPL Horizons offer extraordinary datasets, yet they remain fragmented across static interfaces that force engineers to manually cross-reference tables whenever a launch slips by 48 hours or a lander diverts 50 meters during terminal descent. To bridge this gap between static planetary mapping and agile flight engineering, we created Gravity —an interactive, browser-based lunar landing decision engine that reveals power, thermal, and communication constraints before a spacecraft ever leaves the launchpad. What Gravity Does & How It Works Rather than treating illumination and communication as separate calculations, Gravity fuses lunar topography and orbital mechanics into a unified, real-time workspace. When a mission planner selects a curated Artemis/CLPS candidate site—such as Shackleton Rim, Mons Mouton, or Nobile Rim—or enters custom selenographic coordinates and a target mission epoch, Gravity executes a deterministic physics pipeline directly inside the browser: * Airless Horizon & Terrain Modeling: Using elevation matrices derived from NASA’s Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA), Gravity computes a angular horizon silhouette around the landing point, accounting for true lunar curvature without atmospheric refraction. * Real-Time Ephemeris & Line-of-Sight Computation: Client-side astronomical algorithms calculate exact solar azimuth, solar elevation, surface irradiance , and Earth’s libration analemma across a 29.5-day synodic cycle. By comparing celestial elevation angles against the local LOLA horizon profile at every azimuth step, Gravity determines instantaneously whether solar panels are illuminated and whether Direct-to-Earth (DTE) radio links are open or occluded. * Interactive Temporal Scrubbing & Side-by-Side Comparison: Engineers can drag a live timeline scrubber forward across days or months to watch shadows sweep across crater rims and see blocked Earth links rise back into view—or place two candidate sites side-by-side to weigh power margins against communication windows. * Deterministic Gravity AI Copilot: Embedded within the workspace, Gravity AI translates complex multi-variable telemetry into clear, plain-language operational summaries. Crucially, Gravity AI performs zero generative math; it strictly interprets verified values computed by the client-side physics engine, eliminating AI hallucination while a dedicated Methods audit transparently documents modeling boundaries (such as flat-horizon assumptions outside high-resolution polar datasets). Beyond real-time visualization, Gravity evolves mission planning from passive observation into proactive trade-space optimization through six specialized engineering modules: * Inverse Feasibility Finder: Reverses traditional coordinate guesswork by letting engineers input hardware constraints (such as continuous sunlight, >60\% DTE availability, and terrain slope) to scan South Pole elevation grids and highlight Pareto-optimal landing zones. * Launch Slip Ripple-Effect Simulator (+1 to +60 Days): Models rocket launch delays in real time, recalculating celestial trajectories to trigger Power & Thermal Cliff Alerts when shifting crater shadows threaten battery reserves and automatically recommending resilient "Plan-B" ridges. * 3D Mast & Array Geometry Twin: Models true Above-Ground-Level (AGL) line-of-sight over local micro-relief, proving how raising a solar mast by even 2 meters can clear grazing boulder shadows and extend surface survival. * 100m Terminal Hazard-Avoidance Cone: Evaluates micro-topography across a 100-meter touchdown radius to ensure autonomous hazard-divert maneuvers steer toward sunlit safe zones rather than deadly Micro-PSR (Permanently Shadowed Region) cold traps. * Cryogenic Stress & Multi-Hop Relay Planner: Tracks extreme thermal transitions across shadow boundaries and simulates surface rovers or orbital CubeSats to bridge occluded Earth links via multi-hop geometry. * One-Click CLPS Feasibility Dossier Exporter: Compiles site metrics, horizon profiles, and risk rationales into standardized engineering reports ready for NASA CLPS payload integration reviews. Goals & Mission Benefits Our primary goal is to compress multi-day lunar landing trade studies into seconds while uniting two worlds that often speak different technical languages: planetary scientists, who seek scientifically rich targets near water-ice deposits, and systems engineers, who must protect power, thermal, and telemetry margins. By combining rigorous flight-dynamics telemetry with an intuitive, visual interface, Gravity reduces mission risk for commercial and institutional lunar landers while simultaneously serving as an accessible educational window where students, researchers, and the public can experience the real orbital mechanics of the Artemis generation. Tools, Data, Languages & Software Stack * Space Agency Data & Physics: NASA LRO/LOLA (Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter) digital elevation models, standard lunar ephemeris and libration algorithms, and airless radiative/geometric horizon models. * Front-End & Visualization Architecture: Built with TypeScript, React, and Next.js, utilizing HTML5 Canvas / WebGL for interactive horizon silhouettes, analemma plotting, and real-time 29.5-day synodic timeline rendering. * Styling & UI Engineering: Tailwind CSS and modular component architecture engineered for high-contrast, mission-control readability. * AI & Deployment Infrastructure: Gravity AI integrated via structured prompt-grounding locked strictly to client-side JSON telemetry outputs, deployed continuously on Vercel (lunarhorizon.vercel.app) for instant, zero-install browser execution across desktop and mobile hardware.
